does: Fries crushed raw garlic and chopped fresh coriander in hot fat for a short moment, until the garlic smells sweet and the coriander wilts and darkens, then stirs the sizzling mixture into the pot, most often at the end. It gives a stew, a soup or a dish of pulses a sharp, fresh scent.
how: Crush the garlic with salt to a rough paste, and chop the coriander fine.
Heat the fat in a small pan until it shimmers.
Add the garlic and stir at once. Add the coriander when the garlic turns pale gold and smells sweet.
Take the pan off the heat the moment the coriander has wilted and darkened, and tip it, sizzling, into the pot.
Stir it in and serve soon, while the scent is still bright.

cues.text: A sweet, sharp scent of garlic and green coriander, with no bitter edge.
The garlic is pale gold and never brown, and the coriander has wilted to a dark green.
A lively sizzle as the mixture meets the hot liquid.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the garlic brown, which turns the whole pot bitter.
mistakes.fix: Add the coriander as soon as the garlic turns pale gold, and take the pan off the heat quickly.

mistakes.mistake: Stirring the mixture in early and cooking it on, so that the fresh scent is lost.
mistakes.fix: Add it at the very end, off the heat.

mistakes.mistake: Chopping the coriander coarse, so that stems stay tough.
mistakes.fix: Chop the leaves and tender stems fine.

comes_after.why: The garlic is crushed with salt first, so that it fries evenly and gives its scent at once.

variant_of.differs: The fat holds crushed fresh garlic and chopped fresh coriander and not dry spices. It is cooked for a moment only and is stirred into the pot, most often at the end, so it finishes a dish more than it starts one.
